Directions: Use the information to answer each question that follows.
Content: A student is reading about spacecraft in class. They are surprised to learn that as a spacecraft orbits `text(Earth)` there are small objects in space called debris that can collide with the larger spacecraft and cause damage. They research some information about how scientists have tried to address this problem.

The student learns from their research that to help decrease damage to a spacecraft, scientists designed shields to protect the spacecraft from collisions with space debris. `text(One)` type of shield is called the Stuffed Whipple Shield (SWS). The diagram shows the SWS attached to a spacecraft.

The SWS consists of an aluminum bumper wall, layers of material called Nextel and Kevlar, and an aluminum rear wall closest to the spacecraft. The student also finds a diagram that shows a close-up of the SWS design and how space debris collides with the bumper wall of the SWS.

Scientists ran a simulation building different SWS designs. The data table lists the bumper wall thickness, rear wall thickness, and distance between the bumper wall and rear wall in `text(centimeters)` (`text(cm)`) for four SWS versions.
